display.title: Episode 26: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: After Shavuos, Uncle Yossi explains the flowers and dairy foods of the holiday, brings back the Hakochainik march, and begins the story of Reb Boruch, falsely accused of stealing.
display.summary_long: The first show after Shavuos 5742. Uncle Yossi recalls the holiday: the flowers in shul that remind us of the greenery on Har Sinai, and the dairy foods we eat because the Jewish people, newly given the laws of kashrus, could not yet prepare meat. With the days of Sefirah over, the Hakochainik march returns. An eight-year-old boy leads the Shema in Studio 604, and his proud father thanks Tzivos Hashem. The story, introduced on air as 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik', begins in a small Russian town. Reb Boruch, an honest Chassid who supervises a government lumberyard, is admired by the local minister. Alex, a cruel man fired from the same yard, is consumed by jealousy and hides twenty railroad logs in Reb Boruch's barn, then reports him as a thief. Reb Boruch is summoned to the minister's office for Tuesday morning, a summons from which many never returned. He goes to the Alter Rebbe, who smiles and tells him to come back next Sunday. Trusting the tzaddik, Reb Boruch decides not to go to the minister. A sponsor message and a preview of Parshas Naso close the show.
display.lesson: A tzaddik sees what we cannot; trusting Hashem and following the tzaddik's guidance takes courage, and jealousy leads to terrible hatred.

date.note: Shavuos has just passed; 'be in shul this Shabbos for Parshas Naso' (14 Sivan 5742). Matches the weekly estimate.

advisories.note: A Jew is falsely accused of theft and summoned by the Russian authorities; Jews who received such summonses were jailed or disappeared.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full with his age; his father also speaks.
